title: classroom50/assignments/v1
description: Machine-readable schema for <classroom>/assignments.json, mirroring the authoritative Go validators in cli/gh-teacher (assignments_json.go, tests.go, runtime.go). Intended for non-CLI clients (e.g., the GUI) to validate before writing. Four rules JSON Schema cannot express: (1) test names must be UNIQUE within an assignment, (2) name length is capped at 100 BYTES (UTF-8), not characters, (3) release_assets basenames must be UNIQUE within an assignment, and (4) configured release_assets path strings are capped at 8,192 raw UTF-8 bytes in aggregate — enforce all four client-side. Parser normalizations this schema intentionally rejects include a missing or empty `autograder` (normalized to "default") and `release_assets: null` (normalized to absence) — clients should always write normalized forms, as the CLI does.

assignment.description: One assignment record. additionalProperties is true so a top-level field a newer binary or the web GUI adds survives a read-modify-write verbatim (the 'tolerate AND preserve' rule: CLI via AssignmentEntry.Extra, web via the `...source` spread). Known sub-objects (template/due_meta/runtime, and each tests item) stay closed so a typo inside one is still a hard error.

due.description: RFC 3339 timestamp. The CLI normalizes the teacher's input to a UTC instant (e.g., 2026-09-16T03:59:00Z) and records the original value/zone in `due_meta`; clients should write UTC too. The pattern still permits any offset so older files validate. Advisory: collect-scores compares it against each submission's datetime and marks rows `late` in scores.json; nothing enforces the deadline.

input.description: The due value as supplied (--due flag or migrated source deadline), whitespace-trimmed but otherwise verbatim, before UTC normalization.

zone.description: Best-effort IANA/local zone name; present only when the offset was auto-detected (an explicit offset carries no zone name).

offset.description: Zone offset applied at normalization, e.g., -04:00 (UTC is +00:00).

source.description: How the offset was determined: from the input itself, auto-detected from the machine's local zone, or carried in from a migrated deadline.

due_meta.description: Write-side provenance for `due`, for auditing a wrong-zone deadline. Advisory metadata only -- collect-scores reads `due`, never this.

available_from.description: RFC 3339 timestamp (mirrors `due`): the release date at/after which the assignment is listed on the student's assignments page for everyone. HIDE-BY-DEFAULT: an absent or future value keeps the assignment OFF the student list — students can only accept it via the invite link until the release date passes. A student who has already accepted (their repo exists) always sees it. The CLI normalizes the teacher's input to a UTC instant and records the original value/zone in `available_from_meta`; clients should write UTC too. LISTING-ADVISORY ONLY, not access control: assignments.json is published publicly to GitHub Pages, so a determined student can still read the raw file or a saved accept link — this gates the student UI listing, nothing else.

input.description: The available_from value as supplied (--available-from flag or GUI input), whitespace-trimmed but otherwise verbatim, before UTC normalization.

zone.description: Best-effort IANA/local zone name; present only when the offset was auto-detected (an explicit offset carries no zone name).

offset.description: Zone offset applied at normalization, e.g., -04:00 (UTC is +00:00).

source.description: How the offset was determined: from the input itself, auto-detected from the machine's local zone, or carried in from a migrated value.

available_from_meta.description: Write-side provenance for `available_from` (same shape as `due_meta`), for auditing a wrong-zone release date. Advisory metadata only.

mode.description: `individual` = one repo per student. `group` = a shared repo: the first accepter creates it and becomes its admin, then adds teammates with `gh student invite`. Group size is advisory — `max_group_size` is a coordination hint the founder is expected to respect, NOT a hard security cap. `gh student invite` does apply it as a best-effort guardrail (it refuses to add a collaborator past the cap when run from inside the founder's own group repo), but it is bypassable (the GitHub UI, or simply not running the CLI) — the joiner-driven `gh student group join` that once enforced it was removed. Group mode still REQUIRES `max_group_size` (>= 2) as a contract field for clients like the GUI; individual mode must omit it. See the conditional at the assignment level.

autograder.description: Workflow-shim name; `default` for the universal shim. NOT the grading logic — that's autograder.py or `tests`.

max_group_size.description: Advisory maximum collaborators on a group repo. REQUIRED for `mode: group` (>= 2) and MUST be omitted for `mode: individual`. This is a CONTRACT field, not a hard security ceiling: `gh student invite` enforces it as a best-effort guardrail (refusing to add a collaborator past the cap when run from inside the founder's own group repo), but the check is advisory and bypassable (e.g., adding collaborators via the GitHub UI) — the joiner-side enforcement in `gh student group join` was removed. The founder coordinates actual group size when adding teammates with `gh student invite`. Retained in the schema/assignments.json so clients such as the GUI can display and (optionally) enforce it client-side.

tests.description: Declarative tests. Mutually exclusive with a per-assignment autograder.py at <classroom>/autograders/<slug>/ — probe before writing.

feedback_pr.description: Opt the assignment into the Feedback Pull Request: one long-lived PR per student repo (base = a frozen branch at the baseline commit, head = the default branch) for inline teacher review of the full starter→submission diff. Both accept clients open it at accept time (best-effort, so it exists even with GitHub Actions disabled); the autograde runner adopts that PR by base+head and maintains it, and remains the fallback creator when accept could not. Product default is ON (both `gh teacher assignment add` and the GUI create it enabled). On the wire it is collapsed: the CLI omits the field when false (omitempty), so readers must treat an absent field as `false`; the GUI may also write `false` explicitly, so accept both. Absent or false means the PR never opens.

empty_repo.description: Opt the assignment into truly bare student repos: accept creates the repo with no initial commit (auto_init false) and commits NO control files — no README, no .classroom50.yaml accept marker, no .github/workflows/autograde.yaml shim. Autograding and the Feedback PR are disabled for the assignment; regrade and score collection skip it. Mutually exclusive with template, tests, feedback_pr, allowed_files, release_assets, and pass_threshold (see the conditional at the assignment level). IMMUTABLE after creation: flipping it later would require retrofitting control files into (or stripping them from) every already-accepted student repo, so writers must reject an edit that changes it. On the wire it is collapsed like feedback_pr: the CLI omits the field when false (omitempty), so readers must treat an absent field as `false`; accept an explicit `false` too.

locked.description: Lock the assignment against student access. The web accept page, the student assignments list, the student submission view, and `gh student accept` all refuse a locked assignment for EVERY student, including one who already accepted. UNLIKE available_from (which is listing-advisory only), this is intended as access control — but because assignments.json is published publicly to GitHub Pages, the client gates are still best-effort UX; a determined student can read the raw file. The ENFORCEABLE boundary applies only to a PRIVATE, in-org template: locking also removes the classroom STUDENT team's read on that template repo (teacher/head-TA/TA teams are left untouched), so no new student can generate a repo from it while locked; unlocking re-grants that read. Public-template and template-less assignments can only be UX-gated, never hard-blocked. Existing student repos are not deleted. On the wire it is collapsed like feedback_pr/empty_repo: the CLI omits the field when false (omitempty), so readers must treat an absent field as `false`; accept an explicit `false` too.

allowed_files.description: Ordered .gitignore-style patterns defining which files belong to the submission (order matters, last match wins, `!` re-includes). Example: ["*", "!hello.py"] ignores everything then re-includes hello.py — an allowlist of exactly hello.py. Empty/absent means every file is allowed. The autograde runner enforces it best-effort by removing disallowed working-tree files before grading (control files like .classroom50.yaml and .github/ are always kept), but fails open on git/resource failure — so it is a grading-scope/hygiene tool, not a secret-hiding boundary; `gh student submit` applies it as a best-effort pre-push filter.

release_assets.description: Ordered exact workspace-relative file paths attached to each passing or failing submission Release after grading. Empty/absent disables the feature. Paths must not contain unpaired Unicode surrogates and are flattened to unique Release-safe basenames; writers and runtimes additionally enforce basename uniqueness and an aggregate maximum of 8,192 raw UTF-8 bytes across configured path strings.

pass_threshold.description: Opt-in, advisory passing bar: the integer percentage of max score (0–100) at/above which a gradebook client (e.g., the GUI) shows a submission as passing, plus passing/failing rollups, badges, and filters. ABSENT means the feature is OFF — no passing concept — which is distinct from a 0% threshold; clients must not treat absent as a default. CLI-unenforced like max_group_size: the autograder and score collection never read it; it changes no student's actual score. Written only when a teacher enables it.

student_permission.description: The collaborator role the enrolled student is granted on their OWN assignment repo at accept time (the old GitHub Classroom "grant students admin access" checkbox, generalized to GitHub's full ladder). ABSENT means the built-in default: `push` for `individual`, `admin` for `group`. This is accept-time provisioning only — it governs what NEW accepters get; it does not retroactively change repos already accepted (teachers adjust those with the gradebook's per-repo/bulk access controls). Group coherence: a group founder must hold at least `admin` to add teammates via `gh student invite`, so for `mode: group` any configured value below `admin` is clamped up to `admin` by every accept client — prefer omitting it (or writing `admin`) for group assignments. Caution: on a PRIVATE in-org repo, `admin` also lets the student change repo visibility (e.g. make it public) and settings.

submission_mode.description: When the autograder fires. ABSENT or "every-push" (the default): the student-repo shim triggers on every push to the default branch AND on submit/* tag pushes (the runner mints the submit/<UTC-timestamp>-<short-sha> tag itself on branch pushes). "tag": the shim triggers ONLY on submit/* tag pushes — `gh student submit` pushes the tag after the branch commit (a hand-pushed submit/* tag works too), so a plain `git push` does not grade (the primary Actions-cost lever for large cohorts). Applied to the shim at ACCEPT TIME; changing it later requires retrofitting each existing student repo's shim (`gh teacher assignment submission-mode` or the gradebook bulk action) and students must re-pull afterward. Default-autograder assignments only for the retrofit — teacher-authored (non-default) shims are never rewritten, though the field still governs client tag-pushing. Meaningless for empty_repo (no shim exists) — mutually exclusive (see the conditional at the assignment level). On the wire it is collapsed like feedback_pr: writers omit "every-push" (the CLI normalizes it away), so readers must treat an absent field as "every-push"; accept an explicit "every-push" too. See submission_tags for teacher-named milestone tags; additive room remains for future tags-ignore/branch-pattern fields.

submission_tags.description: Teacher-named milestone tag patterns that ALSO trigger grading — e.g. ["phase1", "phase2", "complete"], or globs like "v*". A student pushing a matching tag (`git tag phase1 && git push origin phase1`) gets that commit graded. TRIGGERS, not records: the runner still mints/reuses the canonical submit/<UTC-timestamp>-<short-sha> tag at the triggering commit and publishes the Release there (immutable one-release-per-submission history; the Release title notes the triggering tag), so collection, regrade, download, and web reads are unaffected. The canonical submit/* namespace ALWAYS triggers too — the generated shim trigger is the union of these patterns and submit/*, and the field is orthogonal to submission_mode (an every-push assignment can also name milestone tags; tag mode drops only the branch trigger). Patterns are the supported subset of GitHub Actions tag filters (literal, `*` not crossing `/`, `**` crossing, `?`, `+`, `[...]`; NO `!` excludes — rejected by writers) rendered verbatim into the shim's on.push.tags, hence the restricted charset (no quotes/whitespace — the values are spliced into a quoted-YAML line). One rule this schema's items.pattern cannot express (it must stay Go-RE2-compilable): validators also reject a LEADING `?`/`+` and a `+` stacked on another quantifier (e.g. `v*+`) — those compile as possessive quantifiers in Python but are errors in Go/JS, so every matcher fails closed on them; clients must apply the same rule (Go ValidateSubmissionTags / web validateSubmissionTags). Like submission_mode, the trigger is baked into each repo's shim at ACCEPT TIME; changing patterns later requires the same shim retrofit, and students must re-pull. Empty/absent means no milestone tags (exactly today's behavior). Caution: a broad glob like "v*" grades every matching release tag a student pushes. Mutually exclusive with empty_repo (no shim exists).

repo_features.description: Per-assignment repository feature overrides applied to each student repo at ACCEPT TIME, on FRESH CREATE only. Each key (issues/wiki/projects/pull_requests) is tri-state: ABSENT = inherit the TEMPLATE's current setting — accept reads the template repo's has_issues/has_wiki/has_projects/has_pull_requests and re-applies them to the student repo, because GitHub's `POST /generate` does NOT copy the template's feature settings (a generated repo otherwise gets GitHub defaults). For a template-less/empty_repo assignment absent is left at GitHub's own create default (no PATCH key is sent — the "Default" choice does not override the feature). `true` = force the feature on, `false` = force it off (an explicit value always wins over the template). Applied via `PATCH /repos/{org}/{repo}`, best-effort/fail-open (a rejection, e.g. org-disabled projects, is logged and does not fail accept). NOT retrofitted to already-accepted repos and NOT re-asserted on re-accept (a student's own later toggle survives); reconcile existing repos with the gradebook bulk action instead. Trust boundary: inheriting a PRIVATE template copies its Issues/Projects/Wiki CONTENT (e.g. a wiki that may hold solutions) into every student repo, so a template used for inherit should not carry cohort-sensitive content. The object is omitted entirely when no key is set.

runtime.description: Omit entirely for the defaults (ubuntu-latest + Python 3.14). Never write empty-string fields. CLOSED CONTRACT: additionalProperties is false and every reader decodes runtime strictly (the CLI's RuntimeRef has no Extra / DisallowUnknownFields; the web rebuilds runtime from the known sub-keys and drops any unknown one on a read-modify-write edit). An unknown sub-key makes the whole file unparseable, so — unlike top-level entry keys, which evolve additively and preserve unknowns — a NEW runtime sub-key must ship in lockstep across this schema, the Go RuntimeRef, and the web Assignment['runtime'] type in the same release; otherwise an older reader silently strips it on edit.

runs-on.description: GitHub Actions runner selection, mirroring Actions' own `runs-on`: a single label string ("ubuntu-latest") or an array of labels (["self-hosted", "gpu"]) for custom / self-hosted runners. No value allow-list — a teacher customizing runs-on owns getting the label right; each label is only anti-injection-checked (1-10 labels). Omit for the default (ubuntu-latest).

name.description: Unique within the assignment (enforce client-side); <= 100 UTF-8 bytes; no control characters.

timeout.description: Seconds, 1-600. 0 (or omitted) means the default of 10s.

points.description: Defaults to 0 (informational test) when omitted; the CLI always writes it.
